title: Supporting the interdisciplinary head and neck tumour board using locally run large language models – a prospective study
summary: Cases of patients diagnosed with malignant tumours are discussed at tumour conferences. Representatives from all the different disciplines involved in assessing and treating the disease attend these conferences. The aim is to develop the best possible treatment plan for each case. Unfortunately, the quality of these conferences varies greatly from hospital to hospital. Due to the large amount of information, it can happen that some information is not given sufficient weight. In such cases, patients may have to be discussed again, resulting in a delay in treatment. Artificial intelligence is already present in many areas of our everyday lives. New language models, known as large language models, have become better known in recent years thanks to services such as ChatGPT. These models can understand human language and answer a wide variety of questions. Their application in medicine is currently being tested in various areas. The models' performance in answering medical questions is very promising. As part of this study, we aim to assess the ability of language models to formulate therapy recommendations for cancer patients. No data will be passed on to an internet-connected programme; it will simply be interpreted by a programme installed on a computer at the University Medical Centre without internet connection. The aim of this study is to determine whether language models can be used to formulate therapy recommendations for tumour patients.
conditions: Patients with tumours in the head and neck area

interventions.name: One group of patients is undergoing treatment at our clinic for a malignant tumour/growth. For this group, a treatment plan is created using a large language model similar to ChatGPT and compared with the doctors' treatment plan.
